settings.openLink: Open this link in a browser on a device in your home network:
settings.serverStopped: The web page is not running.
settings.portInUse: Port __port__ is already used by something else.
settings.accessCodeHelp: Without a code, anyone on your network can view the dashboard. With a code, a browser asks for it once and remembers it. For a tablet on the wall you can also open the address with ?code=… added.
settings.editPinHelp: On the dashboard you change the layout with the pencil at the top right. With a PIN, not everyone on your Wi-Fi can do that.
settings.layoutHelp: Choose which blocks you see, in which order and how wide. You can also do this on the dashboard itself, by dragging. On a phone all blocks are stacked.
settings.layoutCustom: You are using your own layout.
settings.layoutDefault: Default layout: blocks appear by themselves as soon as there is a matching device, such as a home battery or EV charger.
settings.ownHeightHelp: The height was set on the dashboard. Tap to let the content decide it again.
settings.devicesHelp: Leave on "Automatic" to have them found for you.
settings.heating: Heating (heat pump or central heating boiler)
settings.noHeating: No heat pump or central heating boiler found
settings.noBattery: No home battery found yet. Once you add your battery to Homey, it appears here by itself.
settings.invertPower: Battery measures power the other way round
settings.invertPowerHelp: Turn on when charging and discharging are the wrong way round on the dashboard. When your battery has a charging state, the app usually notices by itself.
settings.consumersHelp: The dashboard decides by itself which devices count as a consumer. If a device counts twice (a kWh meter on a circuit and the device behind it), or one is missing, choose that here.
settings.countMeter: looks like a meter for the whole house
settings.countNone: The dashboard leaves out no devices.
settings.boilerTop: Temperature sensor at the top of the tank
settings.boilerBottom: Temperature sensor at the bottom of the tank
settings.coldWaterTemp: Cold water temperature (°C), empty = follows the season
settings.calibrate: Calibrate shower minutes with a button in the shower
settings.calibrateHelp: Off by default. In Flow, add this app's actions "Shower started" and "Shower finished" to your button. From the drop in boiler temperature the app works out the real liters per minute of your shower head and, after 3 showers, uses that instead of the value above.
settings.valve: Three-way valve between water heater and gas boiler
settings.valveHelp: Off by default. For when a Flow switches a three-way valve, so hot tap water comes straight from the water heater or is reheated by the gas boiler. In that Flow, after switching the valve, add this app's action "Hot tap water comes from" and choose the source (a reason is optional). The Heating block then shows where your hot water comes from now and the last three switches. The dashboard cannot see the valve itself: it shows what your Flow commanded, and does not see switching by hand or by another Flow without that action.
settings.tapCheck: Check whether the gas boiler fires for hot tap water
settings.tapCheckHelp: Off by default. For a water heater (such as a heat pump boiler) that preheats the water for a combi boiler, with a sensor or valve that should keep the boiler off while the water heater is hot enough. Needs a water meter, the water heater and a gas meter in Homey. Every 30 seconds the app looks whether water runs while the water heater cools down (a flush or a cold tap does not count) and whether the gas meter then counts more gas than the house used before. The Heating block shows the latest taps and how often the boiler fired while the water heater was hot (from "Hot" from). Short taps that hardly cool the water heater are not seen. When the heating burns during a tap, the result can be "unclear".
settings.tapCheckSinceHelp: Fill in the moment something changed, such as a new sensor. The Heating block then counts the taps before and after that moment apart. Leave it empty to count all together. When turned on, the app also looks back 24 hours in Homey Insights, so a change made today still has a "before".
settings.backupHelp: Every night the app keeps the hours of yesterday (energy and costs) and the finished months, up to 5 years back. Homey Insights keeps old readings ever coarser; with this history the hours stay and net metering and the bill are calculated faster. Export on the dashboard from the screen menu: "Export all hours (CSV)" for a spreadsheet, or "Backup of all data" for everything the app keeps (without your settings). Bring a backup back here, also on another Homey: the logs in the backup replace the app's, the history is filled in.
settings.historyCurrent: The history holds __days__ days per hour and __months__ months, from __from__.
settings.historyEmpty: The history is still empty: the first day goes in after midnight, the finished months within a few minutes.
settings.backupDone: Backup restored: __logs__ logs, __days__ days and __months__ months.
settings.tapCheckPowerHelp: Optional: a smart plug that measures the power of the gas boiler. When the burner starts, the fan runs and the power rises; so the app sees per minute whether the boiler fires, also for short taps. When the boiler was already burning for the heating just before the tap, the gas meter decides. Turn off switching for the plug or hide it: switching it off stops your heating.
settings.tapCheckPower: Power meter of the gas boiler
settings.showerTooCold: The shower temperature must be higher than that of the cold water.
settings.accessCodeLength: Use at least 4 characters for the access code.
settings.contractHelp: All amounts include VAT. Leave a field empty to leave that cost out.
settings.lowHolidaysHelp: Dutch public holidays: New Year's Day, Easter, King's Day, Ascension Day, Whitsun and Christmas, as with most Dutch suppliers.
settings.exportRateHelp: With net metering (salderen, until 2027) this is usually the same as the normal rate.
settings.nettingHelp: Export is then credited at the price you pay at that moment. Ends on 1 January 2027.
settings.nettingOrder: Net metering with normal and off-peak rate
settings.nettingOrderHelp: Most suppliers set export off against what you imported at the normal rate first. Some do it per counter: export in off-peak hours against off-peak.
settings.supplierHelp: Price per quarter hour = market price + energy tax + markup. The energy tax of 2026 is filled in.
settings.monthlyHelp: Supply and network costs together, as on your bill. The reduction is deducted spread over the year.
settings.billHelp: For the Yearly bill block: whether you will pay extra or get money back. The start of your billing year is the date your last yearly bill started; empty is 1 January. The end of your contract is optional.
settings.previousHelp: Optional, normal and off-peak together. As long as the dashboard has not measured a year, it estimates the missing months with this use: what is left after the measured months, gas spread by degree days.
settings.startImport: Import reading at start of billing year (kWh)
settings.startExport: Export reading at start of billing year (kWh)
settings.startGas: Gas reading at start of billing year (m³)
settings.startReadingsHelp: Optional: the final readings on your last yearly bill, normal and off-peak added up. The use from before the dashboard measured then counts as measured: the readings now minus these.
settings.forecastHelp: From Forecast.Solar (free), for the location of your Homey. Shown as a dashed line in "Power today". Off, with the app PV Forecast installed: its expected kWh for today and tomorrow are shown, without a line.
settings.checkPrices: Check all amounts against your own contract or your supplier's app. The suggested values are only a starting point: suppliers change their markups, and the dashboard only calculates correctly with your own amounts.
settings.supplierConfirmed: __name__ publishes these amounts on its own website (checked in September 2026). They can have changed since: check them on your contract.
settings.supplierPartly: __name__ publishes the electricity markup on its own website (checked in September 2026); the gas markup comes from a comparison site. Check both on your contract.
settings.supplierUnconfirmed: __name__ does not publish its markup openly; these amounts come from a comparison site (September 2026). Look them up on your contract or in the __name__ app and change them.
settings.supplierNoGas: The gas markup is not known: fill it in yourself.
settings.taxReductionMonthly: The energy tax reduction is a yearly amount (2026: about € 629). This looks like a monthly amount: fill in the yearly amount or leave the field empty.
settings.exportFeeHigh: An export fee is usually a few cents per kWh. This is about half your electricity price or more: is that right?
settings.supplierOther: Fill in your supplier's markup yourself; you find it on your contract or in its app.
settings.alertHours: Warn when a device is on for longer than (hours)
settings.alertNotifyHelp: Each warning at most once a day. Devices that are always on (fridge, network) are left out by themselves.
settings.exportAfterHelp: What your supplier pays per exported kWh from 2027. Empty: the legal minimum, half of the supply price without energy tax.
settings.currencyHelp: The currency of the amounts on the dashboard and here. Automatic takes the one of Homey Energy, or euro when Homey does not give one. Amounts are not converted; EnergyZero gives Dutch prices in euro.
settings.sourceAuto: Automatic: Homey when it has dynamic prices, otherwise EnergyZero
settings.sourcePowerhour: Power by the Hour (the prices of that app, with its markups)
settings.sourceInUseHomey: In use now: the dynamic prices of Homey Energy.
settings.sourceInUseEnergyZero: In use now: EnergyZero, the Dutch market price including VAT.
settings.sourceInUsePowerhour: In use now: the prices of Power by the Hour, all-in with the markups entered there. A dynamic contract below then only counts for the fixed costs.
settings.powerhourMissing: Power by the Hour is not installed, so EnergyZero is used.
settings.homeyFormula: Homey calculates with your costs: __formula__. That formula makes the all-in price; the markup and energy tax below then do not count.
settings.homeyNoFormula: Homey has no costs set for its dynamic prices yet, so the dashboard uses the contract below. Homey gives the market price without VAT; the dashboard adds 21% VAT to it.
settings.homeyFixed: Homey has a fixed price of __price__ per kWh; it counts when you leave the rate below empty.
settings.homeyNoPrices: Homey Energy has no prices. Set them up under Energy → Settings in the Homey app.
settings.capacityHelp: For Belgium: you pay for your highest quarter-hour power each month, averaged over 12 months and at least 2.5 kW. With a tariff the Monthly peak block shows the cost, and the dashboard warns when a quarter hour goes above your monthly peak. Leave empty in the Netherlands.
settings.planesHelp: For example east and west, or the garage roof as well. Up to 10 roof planes; Forecast.Solar calculates each one separately.
settings.manual: Manual (in Dutch): what each block shows and every setting ↗
settings.shareHelp: Something not working well with your devices, such as a battery or inverter that is not found? Send a report to the maker of the app. It holds which apps and readings your devices have and their current values, without names, rooms, location or address. It shows below and in the e-mail or issue, and is only sent when you press Send there.
settings.shareCopied: The report is on your clipboard. If it is not in the e-mail or issue that opens now, paste it in.
settings.shareIssueIntro: What does not work well? (for example: my battery is not found)
settings.sharePaste: (Paste the report here; it is on your clipboard.)
settings.shareSnapshotHelp: This lets the maker see exactly what you see, to fix a display problem. Device names and today's use are included then. The report is then too big for the e-mail itself: paste it from your clipboard.
settings.groupsHelp: For the Circuits block: add your circuits with their fuse and the phase they are on, and give every device with a power meter the circuit it is on. For devices without a meter whose use stays about the same (modem, switch) enter a fixed use. What the circuits together do not explain is shown per phase as Other.
settings.groupDevicesHelp: Which circuit is each device on? Is a device on more circuits, such as a Perilex hob on two, choose the second circuit too: its power then counts half on each circuit.
settings.groupFixedHelp: Optional. For what hangs on this circuit without a meter of its own, such as a router or fridge: enter your estimate in watts. A device without a meter that has a use set in Homey (Advanced settings, Energy) can also be given this circuit below; it then counts with that use. It is added to the measured power. Nothing like that? Leave it empty.
settings.groupsSolarHelp: For Other per phase: your smart meter measures import minus export per phase, so the block adds the solar power on a phase back to it.
settings.groupsBatteryHelp: For Other per phase: what the battery charges is taken off that phase, and what it delivers is added, like solar power. A plug-in battery is usually on one phase. Unknown? Leave it on all three.
settings.importHelp: Homey keeps the use per quarter hour for only a month. If you have a HomeWizard P1 meter with Energy+, export a year per 15 minutes in the HomeWizard Energy app (Settings → Graphs → electricity → Export graph data) and choose that file here. When it was dark is calculated from the height of the sun, matched to the nights Homey measures itself. Measured nights always come first.
settings.importDone: Done: __nights__ nights from __from__ to __to__ (__skipped__ skipped for missing or implausible readings).
settings.webPinHelp: Enter the edit PIN you set for Energy Dashboard in the Homey app. Without a PIN the settings can only be changed in Homey.
settings.homeyOnly: The port, access code and edit PIN can only be changed in the Homey app, not on this web page.
settings.groupExtras: Devices that are not in Homey
settings.groupExtrasHelp: Optional. For a device that is not connected to Homey, such as a fridge or a freezer: give it a name and an average use in watts, and choose its circuit below. It always counts with that use (with ≈ in the block). A device that switches on and off is better added to Homey with a use when on and off, for example as a virtual device.
